description: A threshold-triggered looper: a control signal above the threshold makes it record half a second of the input and then play a chosen slice of it over and over until the control signal falls again

params.text: Scales the end control input before it is added to the END knob
Scales the start control input before it is added to the START knob
Sets where in the recorded half second the loop ends, from a hundredth of the way in to the far end
Sets where in the recorded half second the loop starts, from the beginning to the far end
Sets the voltage the control signal has to pass before recording starts, 0 to 10V
Sets how long the crossfade at the loop point lasts, from one sample to about three thousand, which softens the click of the jump

inputs.text: The signal to be recorded and looped; it is not passed through, so the module works as a send rather than an insert
Added to the END knob through the END CV knob, a tenth of the recording per volt at full amount
Added to the START knob through the START CV knob, a tenth of the recording per volt at full amount
The signal watched against the threshold: rising past it starts the recording, and falling back below it ends the loop

outputs.text: The looped slice of the recording, one channel, clamped to -10V and +10V

notes: the module does nothing until the threshold jack is fed something that goes above the THRESHOLD knob; with that jack empty it reads 0V and never fires
no audio passes through: the output carries the loop alone, so patch it as a send rather than in line
once the loop is running the START and END controls can be moved freely, and setting the end before the start plays the slice backwards
the module is monophonic and records at whatever the engine's sample rate is, always half a second's worth

inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.3:
0 to 10V · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
